A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 25 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including their appendices, equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FEM-based experiments on 2D and 3D inverse material design, baseline comparisons, ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original material-design experiments with revised guidance, an additional reinforcement-learning comparison, diversity measurements and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Section 6.2 replaces v1's separate gradient multipliers for E and nu (0.5 and 0.02) with normalization-derivative scaling, gradient-norm clipping at 2.5 and clipping of the predicted clean sample during guidance. These refine inference within the retained diffusion/FEM/backprojection method; the architecture and objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same reported 500-material MatWeb setup, 2D and 3D matrix-particle design tasks, bulk-modulus targets and additional density-minimization objective. Sampling details moved to Appendix A do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds an evaluated soft actor-critic reinforcement-learning baseline across the five 2D bulk-modulus targets, substantially extending comparison to another optimization approach (Table 1; Appendix F). Bayesian optimization and conditional diffusion remain. Unguided sampling and the projection variant were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces full-design-parameter entropy as an evaluation metric throughout the principal comparisons. It also adds an RL protocol with ten-step episodes, one spatial arrangement during training, ten during evaluation and results from the 35,000-interaction checkpoint. Guidance settings change, while retained diffusion-training budgets, target selection and 200-sample evaluations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 9 replaces the E/nu scaling sweep with a sweep over guidance strength and maximum gradient norm. New Figure 10 analyzes guidance strength against accuracy and diversity. Existing dataset-size, denoising-step, projection, density-weight and backprojection analyses remain, with updated evidence; projection results additionally appear by target.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and appendix standard deviations over three seeds, with aggregate ablation deviations also spanning five targets. v2 extends this practice to additional results and metrics. No changed repeated-run count for retained experiments, new confidence intervals or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Guided results change extensively under revised guidance: mean 2D frac within 5% changes from 0.226 to 0.309 (v1 Table 4a; v2 Table 2a), while 3D frac within 1% at K*=330.3 changes from 0.100 to 0.047 (v1 Table 1b; v2 Table 3). Projection changes from reducing average material coverage to increasing it. RL, entropy and target-specific projection results are added. These are revised-configuration results, not fixed-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix B defines ent as the mean entropy in bits over parameter-space discretizations using 2^1 through 2^6 bins per dimension. This adds a mathematical metric definition. The implicit-differentiation derivation, optimization formulation and assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly frames novelty as combining existing components and adds a claim of diverse solutions within 5% relative error across all tested targets. The central claims of 1% accuracy for medium-to-high targets and adaptable multi-objective guidance remain.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies training-seed robustness as strongest at well-performing targets and acknowledges substantial variability at difficult targets. Appendix E adds a warning that new problems may require guidance retuning and explains excessive guidance as overwhelming diffusion regularization. The linear-FEM applicability boundaries remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project code-availability statement and repository address, revised guidance instructions, entropy calibration details and SAC implementation settings, including target entropy 4, discount 0.9 and 16 gradient steps per interaction. Existing architecture and hardware documentation remains; Appendix A still states that datasets and models cannot be publicly released.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Haarnoja et al. for SAC and Raffin et al. for Stable-Baselines3. It more explicitly acknowledges existing methodological components and distinguishes target-specific RL training from inference-time objective flexibility. The broader related-work coverage remains stable.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify material terminology, contributions and experimental findings. Model and training descriptions are combined, sampling details move to Appendix A, and evaluation details receive a dedicated Appendix B. The main section sequence and most methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the result displays: separate 2D method and baseline tables become a unified comparison, 3D results receive their own table, and entropy columns extend the main and uncertainty tables. Figure 9 has different axes and content, Figure 10 adds three sensitivity plots, and qualitative sample montages are replaced.

improvement.justification: The tuned RL comparison, full-parameter diversity metric and guidance-strength analysis strengthen evidence for the central accuracy-diversity claims. More qualified robustness discussion and documented code access improve transparency. These are incremental gains over v1's substantial existing evaluation. Performance changes are mixed under revised guidance, and the data/model-release restrictions remain.
